docs.title: HydroDHM
docs.text:
Differentiable Hydrological Model for Data-Scarce Basins

HydroDHM is a PyTorch-based differentiable hydrological modeling framework designed for data-scarce basins. It provides both physics-based models (XAJ) and deep learning models (LSTM, DPL-XAJ) with command-line tools for easy deployment.

docs.title: 🏔️ Physics-Based Models
docs.text:
• XAJ Model: Xin'anjiang hydrological model with automatic calibration
  • Multiple Algorithms: SCE-UA, GA, scipy optimization
  • Command-Line Tools: No coding required

docs.title: 🧠 Deep Learning Models
docs.text:
• LSTM: Pure data-driven neural networks
  • DPL-XAJ: Hybrid physics-constrained deep learning
  • Automatic Training: Simple YAML configuration

docs.title: 📊 Comprehensive Analysis
docs.text:
• Multiple evaluation metrics (NSE, KGE, RMSE, PBIAS)
  • Publication-quality visualizations
  • Multi-basin analysis support

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/OuyangWenyu/HydroDHM.git
cd HydroDHM

# Install with uv (recommended)
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
uv sync

docs.title: Run XAJ Model
docs.text:
cd hydrodhm/run_xaj
python calibrate_xaj_unified.py --config config_camels.yaml
python evaluate_xaj_unified.py --exp your_experiment
python visualize_unified.py --eval-dir results/your_experiment/evaluation_test

docs.title: Train LSTM Model
docs.text:
cd hydrodhm/run_lstm
python train_lstm.py --config config_lstm_camels.yaml

docs.text: Model Type Pros Best For XAJ Physics-based Interpretable, fewer parameters Physical understanding LSTM Deep learning High accuracy, data-driven Large datasets DPL-XAJ Hybrid Physics + ML Best of both worlds

docs.title: Methods Section Example
docs.text: We used HydroDHM (Ouyang et al., 2024), a differentiable hydrological modeling framework, to calibrate the XAJ model and train LSTM neural networks for streamflow prediction. The models were evaluated on the CAMELS dataset using NSE, KGE, and RMSE metrics.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Learn how to configure HydroDHM for your specific needs.

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
HydroDHM uses two types of configuration:

  1. Global Configuration: hydro_setting.yml (in home directory)
  2. Model Configuration: YAML files for specific experiments

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
WindowsmacOS/Linux 
C:\Users\YourUsername\hydro_setting.yml

~/hydro_setting.yml

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
local_data_path:
  # Root directory for all data
  root: 'D:\data'

  # Original datasets
  datasets-origin: 'D:\data'

  # Processed datasets
  datasets-interim: 'D:\data'

  # Cache directory
  cache: 'D:\data\.cache'

# Optional: Specific dataset paths
camels_us: 'D:\data\camels_us'
selfmadehydrodataset: 'D:\data\my_basins'

docs.title: Minimal Configuration
docs.text:
data:
  dataset: "camels_us"
  basin_ids: ["01013500"]
  train_period: ["1990-10-01", "2000-09-30"]
  test_period: ["2000-10-01", "2010-09-30"]
  output_dir: "results"
  experiment_name: "my_experiment"

model:
  name: "xaj_mz"

training:
  algorithm: "SCE_UA"
  loss: "RMSE"
  SCE_UA:
    rep: 5000
    ngs: 100

evaluation:
  metrics: ["NSE", "KGE", "RMSE"]

docs.title: Full Configuration
docs.text: See config_camels.yaml for all options.

docs.title: LSTM Configuration
docs.text:
data:
  dataset: "camels_us"
  basin_ids: ["01013500", "01022500"]
  train_period: ["2000-10-01", "2010-09-30"]
  test_period: ["2012-10-01", "2015-09-30"]

  forcing_vars:
    - "precipitation"
    - "temperature_max"
    - "temperature_min"

  target_vars:
    - "streamflow"

model:
  name: "CpuLSTM"
  params:
    n_hidden_states: 256
    seq_length: 270

training:
  use_gpu: false
  epochs: 50
  batch_size: 256
  optimizer: "Adam"

docs.title: DPL-XAJ Configuration
docs.text:
data:
  dataset: "camels_us"
  forcing_vars:
    - "precipitation"
    - "potential_evapotranspiration"
  target_vars:
    - "streamflow"
    - "evapotranspiration"

model:
  name: "DplAttrXaj"
  params:
    n_output_features: 15  # XAJ parameters
    warmup_length: 30

training:
  use_gpu: true
  batch_size: 50
  optimizer: "Adadelta"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
You can override the config file location:

export HYDRO_SETTING_FILE=/path/to/custom/hydro_setting.yml

docs.title: Command-Line Overrides
docs.text:
Most parameters can be overridden via command line:

# XAJ
python calibrate_xaj_unified.py \
    --config config.yaml \
    --output-dir custom_results \
    --experiment-name my_exp

# LSTM
python train_lstm.py \
    --config config.yaml \
    --epochs 100 \
    --batch-size 512 \
    --gpu-id 0 1

docs.title: Configuration Validation
docs.text:
Validate your configuration before running:

# XAJ dry run
python calibrate_xaj_unified.py --config config.yaml --dry-run

# Check configuration programmatically
python -c "
import yaml
with open('config.yaml') as f:
    config = yaml.safe_load(f)
    print('✓ Configuration valid')
    print(f'Basins: {config[\"data\"][\"basin_ids\"]}')
"

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Start Small

Test with 1-2 basins and short periods first

Path Format

  • Windows: Use 'D:\path' or 'D:/path'
  • Linux/macOS: Use '/path/to/data'

Backup Configs

Save successful configurations for reproducibility

docs.text: Get up and running with HydroDHM in minutes!

docs.text:
HydroDHM offers three types of models:

XAJ (Physics)LSTM (Deep Learning)DPL-XAJ (Hybrid)

docs.title: Models Overview
docs.text: HydroDHM provides three types of hydrological models, each with distinct advantages.

docs.title: 1. XAJ (Xin'anjiang Model)
docs.text:
Type: Physics-based conceptual model

Key Features: - Based on physical hydrological processes - Interpretable parameters - Well-established in hydrology community - Fast calibration

Best For: - Physical understanding of catchment behavior - Limited data scenarios - Traditional hydrological analysis - Parameter regionalization

Learn more →

docs.title: 2. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory)
docs.text:
Type: Pure deep learning

Key Features: - Data-driven neural network - Captures complex nonlinear relationships - No prior hydrological knowledge needed - State-of-the-art accuracy

Best For: - Large datasets (many basins, long records) - Pure prediction tasks - When physical interpretation is not critical - Benchmark comparisons

Learn more →

docs.title: 3. DPL-XAJ (Differentiable Parameter Learning + XAJ)
docs.text:
Type: Hybrid physics-constrained deep learning

Key Features: - Combines LSTM with XAJ model - Neural network learns XAJ parameters - Physics-based constraints - Interpretable and accurate

Best For: - When you want both accuracy and interpretability - Limited data with physical constraints - Understanding hydrological processes with ML - Research on hybrid modeling

Learn more →

docs.title: Performance Comparison
docs.text:
Based on CAMELS-US experiments (671 basins):

Model NSE (Median) Training Time Interpretability Data Requirements XAJ 0.65 Minutes ★★★★★ Low LSTM 0.75 Hours ★ High DPL-XAJ 0.73 Days ★★★★ Medium

docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Choose Model] --> B{Need Interpretation?}
    B -->|Yes| C{Have enough data?}
    B -->|No| D{Large dataset?}
    C -->|Yes| E[DPL-XAJ]

docs.title: Decision Flowchart
docs.text:
Start here:

  1. Do you need physical interpretation?
  2. Yes → Go to 2

  3. No → Go to 3

  4. Do you have sufficient training data (>50 basins or >10 years)?

  5. Yes → DPL-XAJ (best of both worlds)

  6. No → XAJ (traditional calibration)

  7. Do you have large datasets (>100 basins, >20 years)?

  8. Yes → LSTM (highest accuracy)
  9. No → XAJ (reliable baseline)

docs.title: XAJ Model
docs.text:
Parameters (15): - K, B, IM, WM, WUM, WLM, C, SM, EX, KI, KG, A, θ, CI, CG

Inputs: - Precipitation - Potential evapotranspiration

Outputs: - Streamflow - Soil moisture states - Evapotranspiration

docs.title: LSTM Model
docs.text:
Architecture: - Input: Forcings + Basin attributes - LSTM layers (256 hidden units) - Output: Streamflow

Inputs (configurable): - Precipitation - Temperature (min/max) - Radiation - Vapor pressure - +Basin attributes

Outputs: - Streamflow

docs.title: DPL-XAJ Model
docs.text:
Architecture: - LSTM → Parameter network → XAJ model

Inputs: - Precipitation - Potential ET - Basin attributes

Outputs: - Streamflow - XAJ parameters (dynamic) - Intermediate states

docs.title: Computational Requirements
docs.text: Model CPU GPU Memory Storage XAJ ✓ - <1 GB <100 MB LSTM ✓ Recommended 2-8 GB 1-5 GB DPL-XAJ ✓ Required 4-16 GB 2-10 GB

docs.title: Deep Learning Models for Streamflow Prediction
docs.text: This document provides detailed information about the deep learning models available in HydroDHM.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
HydroDHM provides two types of deep learning models:

  1. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory): Pure data-driven neural network
  2. DPL-XAJ (Differentiable Parameter Learning + XAJ): Hybrid physics-constrained model

Both models are built on the torchhydro framework.

docs.title: LSTM Model
docs.text:
Architecture: 

Input (Forcings + Attributes)
    ↓
LSTM Layers (256 hidden units)
    ↓
Dense Layer
    ↓
Output (Streamflow)

Key Features: - Sequence-to-sequence learning - Handles temporal dependencies - Can incorporate static basin attributes - Fast training on GPU

When to Use: - Large datasets (hundreds of basins, years of data) - Pure prediction tasks - When interpretability is not critical

docs.title: DPL-XAJ Model
docs.text:
Architecture: 

Input (Forcings + Attributes)
    ↓
LSTM Layers (256 hidden units)
    ↓
Parameter Network (15 XAJ parameters)
    ↓
XAJ Hydrological Model (Physics-based)
    ↓
Output (Streamflow + ET)

Key Features: - Neural network learns XAJ parameters dynamically - Physics-based constraints from XAJ model - Interpretable parameters - Requires warmup period for hydrological states

When to Use: - Need physical interpretability - Limited data scenarios - Want to understand hydrological processes - Combine data-driven and physics-based approaches

docs.title: LSTM Configuration
docs.text:
data:
  dataset: "camels_us"
  basin_ids: ["01013500", "01022500"]
  train_period: ["2000-10-01", "2010-09-30"]
  test_period: ["2012-10-01", "2015-09-30"]

  forcing_vars:
    - "precipitation"
    - "temperature_max"
    - "temperature_min"
    - "daylight_duration"
    - "solar_radiation"
    - "vapor_pressure"

  target_vars:
    - "streamflow"

model:
  name: "CpuLSTM"  # or "CudnnLSTM" for GPU
  params:
    n_input_features: 23    # Forcings + attributes
    n_output_features: 1     # Streamflow only
    n_hidden_states: 256     # LSTM hidden size
    seq_length: 270          # Lookback window (days)

training:
  use_gpu: false
  epochs: 50
  batch_size: 256
  optimizer: "Adam"
  loss_func: "RMSESum"
  lr_scheduler:
    0: 0.001
    10: 0.0005
    20: 0.0001

docs.title: DPL-XAJ Configuration
docs.text:
data:
  dataset: "camels_us"
  basin_ids: ["01013500", "01022500"]
  train_period: ["1985-10-01", "1995-09-30"]
  test_period: ["2000-10-01", "2010-09-30"]

  forcing_vars:
    - "precipitation"
    - "potential_evapotranspiration"

  target_vars:
    - "streamflow"
    - "evapotranspiration"  # Auxiliary output

model:
  name: "DplAttrXaj"
  params:
    n_input_features: 17     # Forcings + attributes
    n_output_features: 15    # XAJ parameters
    n_hidden_states: 256
    kernel_size: 15          # XAJ routing kernel
    seq_length: 60           # Forecast horizon
    warmup_length: 30        # Hydrological warmup
    param_limit_func: "clamp"

training:
  use_gpu: true  # Strongly recommended
  epochs: 50
  batch_size: 50  # Smaller than LSTM
  optimizer: "Adadelta"
  loss_func: "RMSESum"
  loss_weights: [1, 0]  # [streamflow, ET]

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Data
docs.text:
Ensure hydro_setting.yml is configured:

local_data_path:
  datasets-origin: 'D:/data'
  cache: 'D:/data/.cache'

docs.title: Step 2: Edit Configuration
docs.text:
Choose and modify a config template:

cd hydrodhm/run_lstm
cp config_lstm_camels.yaml my_lstm_config.yaml
# Edit my_lstm_config.yaml

docs.title: Step 3: Train Model
docs.text:
# LSTM
python train_lstm.py --config my_lstm_config.yaml

# DPL-XAJ
python train_dpl_xaj.py --config my_dpl_config.yaml

docs.title: Step 4: Monitor Training
docs.text:
Training progress is saved in the output directory:

results/
└── my_experiment/
    ├── train_log.txt          # Training logs
    ├── model_epoch_10.pth     # Model checkpoints
    ├── model_epoch_20.pth
    └── best_model.pth         # Best model

docs.title: Important Hyperparameters
docs.text:
LSTM: - n_hidden_states (128-512): Larger = more capacity, slower training - seq_length (60-365): Longer = more context, more memory - batch_size (64-512): Larger = faster, more memory - learning_rate (0.0001-0.01): Start with 0.001

DPL-XAJ: - warmup_length (30-365): Longer = better physics initialization - kernel_size (5-30): Controls routing time scale - batch_size (20-100): Smaller due to memory requirements - loss_weights: Balance between streamflow and ET

docs.title: Recommended Settings
docs.text:
Small dataset (<10 basins): 

n_hidden_states: 128
batch_size: 64
epochs: 100

Medium dataset (10-100 basins): 

n_hidden_states: 256
batch_size: 256
epochs: 50

Large dataset (>100 basins): 

n_hidden_states: 512
batch_size: 512
epochs: 30

docs.title: Performance Comparison
docs.text:
Based on CAMELS-US experiments:

Model NSE (median) Training Time Interpretability XAJ (calibrated) 0.65 Fast (minutes) High LSTM 0.75 Medium (hours) Low DPL-XAJ 0.73 Slow (days) High

Key Insights: - LSTM achieves best raw performance - DPL-XAJ offers physics interpretability with near-LSTM performance - XAJ is fastest but needs careful calibration

docs.title: Multi-GPU Training
docs.text:
For large-scale experiments:

# Use multiple GPUs
python train_lstm.py --config config.yaml --gpu-id 0 1 2 3

docs.title: Transfer Learning
docs.text:
Use pretrained model on new basins:

training:
  pretrained_model: "results/pretrained/best_model.pth"
  freeze_layers: ["lstm"]  # Only train output layer

docs.title: Custom Loss Functions
docs.text:
Combine multiple objectives:

training:
  loss_func: "MultiOutLoss"
  loss_weights: [0.7, 0.3]  # [NSE, KGE]

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
1. Out of Memory (OOM) 

RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
Solutions: - Reduce batch_size - Reduce seq_length - Reduce n_hidden_states - Use gradient accumulation

2. NaN Loss 

Loss becomes NaN during training
Solutions: - Reduce learning rate - Check for missing data in inputs - Use gradient clipping - Verify data normalization

3. Slow Convergence 

Model not improving after many epochs
Solutions: - Increase learning rate - Check data quality - Add more training data - Try different optimizer (Adam vs Adadelta)

4. Poor Generalization 

Good training metrics, poor test metrics
Solutions: - Reduce model complexity (fewer hidden units) - Add dropout - Use more training data - Check for data leakage

docs.title: Data Preprocessing
docs.text:
1. Remove bad basins: Check for data quality issues
  2. Normalize inputs: Use DapengScaler for hydrology
  3. Handle missing data: Interpolate or mask
  4. Split data carefully: Avoid temporal leakage

docs.title: Training Strategy
docs.text:
1. Start small: Test on 1-2 basins first
  2. Use validation set: Monitor overfitting
  3. Save checkpoints: Don't lose progress
  4. Log everything: Track hyperparameters and metrics

docs.title: Model Selection
docs.text:
1. LSTM: Best for pure prediction, large datasets
  2. DPL-XAJ: Best for interpretability, physics constraints
  3. XAJ: Best for traditional hydrology, fast calibration

docs.title: Deep Learning Models Introduction
docs.text:
HydroDHM provides two deep learning models for streamflow prediction:

  1. LSTM: Pure data-driven neural network
  2. DPL-XAJ: Hybrid physics-constrained model

Both are built on torchhydro.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text: ✓ High Accuracy: State-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets ✓ Temporal Dependencies: Excellent at capturing time series patterns ✓ Scalability: Train once on many basins ✓ Transfer Learning: Apply to ungauged basins

docs.title: Challenges
docs.text: ✗ Data Hungry: Requires substantial training data ✗ Black Box: Limited interpretability (pure LSTM) ✗ Computational: Needs GPU for reasonable speed ✗ Overfitting Risk: Can memorize instead of generalize

docs.title: LSTM
docs.text:
Pure Data-Driven

Inputs → LSTM Layers → Dense → Streamflow

Pros: - Highest raw accuracy - Fast training - No hydrological knowledge needed

Cons: - Black box - Requires large datasets - May violate physical constraints

docs.title: DPL-XAJ
docs.text:
Physics-Constrained

Inputs → LSTM → XAJ Parameters → XAJ Model → Streamflow

Pros: - Physically interpretable - Works with less data - Respects hydrological constraints - Dynamic parameter learning

Cons: - Slower training - More complex setup - Requires GPU

docs.title: When to Use Each
docs.text: Scenario Recommended Model Large dataset (>100 basins, >20 years) LSTM Need physical interpretation DPL-XAJ Limited data (<10 years) DPL-XAJ or XAJ Pure prediction task LSTM Research on hybrid modeling DPL-XAJ Operational forecasting LSTM (if data available)

docs.title: Quick Start: LSTM
docs.text:
cd hydrodhm/run_lstm
python train_lstm.py --config config_lstm_camels.yaml --epochs 5

docs.title: Quick Start: DPL-XAJ
docs.text:
cd hydrodhm/run_lstm
python train_dpl_xaj.py --config config_dpl_camels.yaml --epochs 5

docs.title: Sequence Length
docs.text:
How many past time steps the model looks at:

  • LSTM: 270 days typical
  • DPL-XAJ: 60 days typical (+ warmup)

docs.title: Warmup Period
docs.text:
For DPL-XAJ, initialize hydrological states:

  • Typical: 30-365 days
  • Purpose: Let XAJ model "spin up"

docs.title: Batch Size
docs.text:
Number of samples processed together:

  • LSTM: 256-512 typical
  • DPL-XAJ: 50-100 (memory intensive)

docs.title: Hidden Units
docs.text:
LSTM layer size:

  • Small models: 128
  • Medium: 256
  • Large: 512

docs.title: Performance Examples
docs.text:
Based on CAMELS-US (671 basins):

LSTM Results: - Median NSE: 0.75 - Training time: ~12 hours (V100 GPU) - Inference: < 1 second per basin

DPL-XAJ Results: - Median NSE: 0.73 - Training time: ~48 hours (V100 GPU) - Inference: < 2 seconds per basin
